newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-COVENTRY CUP WOES CONTINUE AGAINST WOKING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COVENTRY CUP WOES CONTINUE AGAINST WOKING.

text.p: Woking wrote another memorable chapter in their history while Coventry came close to experiencing another cup nightmare when the minor league side held their premier league opponents to a 1-1 draw in the F.A. Cup on Saturday.
With just seconds remaining of the third round tie, the 1000-1 outsiders scored through Steve Thompson to cancel out Eoin Jess's 75th minute strike.
Since winning the Cup for the only time in 1987 Coventry have never progressed beyond the fourth round, the worst moment coming when they lost to minor league Sutton in the third round in 1989.

They now face a tough replay at Woking on February 4 and it is not beyond the realms of possibility that Woking could add the Sky Blues to their list of league scalps which include West Bromwich (1991), and Millwall and Cambridge this season.

Hednesford, the only other minor league side in the Cup, gave Bryan Robson's Middlesbrough the fright of their lives when Joe O'Connor put the little club from the Midlands ahead after 14 minutes of their fourth round tie. The premier league side were then made to work very hard for their 3-2 victory.
Middlesbrough pulled level through a 26th minute own goal but went ahead for the first time only four minutes from the end when Norwegian substitute Jan-Aage Fjortoft scored.

Unsettled Italian Fabrizio Ravanelli, whose 42,000 pounds sterling ($68,400) weekly salary could buy and sell the entire Hednesford club several times over, made it 3-1 with two minutes to go. But O'Connor had the last word with a second in the last minute.

If ultimately Hednesford scored only a moral victory there were tangible upset successes for first division Bradford, who beat Everton 3-2 in a fourth round tie at Goodison Park, and second division Wrexham, who beat hapless West Ham 1-0 in a third round replay at Upton Park.

Bradford, struggling near the bottom of division one, sent Everton reeling to their sixth defeat in seven matches thanks to an inspired performance by Chris Waddle, a losing finalist with Tottenham 10 years ago.
Waddle had a hand in all three goals which came in a 10-minute spell, scoring the second himself in the 51st minute soon after John Dreyer had put Bradford ahead.

An own goal put Everton back in the match before Rob Steiner restored Bradford's two-goal advantage in the 59th minute. Gary Speed scored in the last minute for Everton but that could not stop Bradford reaching the fifth round for the first time since 1988.

Wrexham, who scored a famous Cup win over Arsenal five years ago, upset another side from the capital thanks to a last-minute winner from substitute Kevin Russell. He powered home a 20-metre drive to send more than 3,000 travelling fans wild with delight.

In contrast, angry home fans hurled abuse at the directors' box at the end. The Hammers have won only once in their last 16 games and face an uphill struggle to avoid relegation. Manager Harry Redknapp offered his resignation after the match.

Cup holders Manchester United, without David Beckham, David May, Nicky Butt, Ronny Johnsen and Gary Pallister, looked to have secured their passage into the fifth round when Paul Scholes found the net with a low diving header after 89 minutes to put them 1-0 up against fellow premier league rivals Wimbledon.
But the London side, who have lost only two of their last 26 matches, came storming back with a header from Robbie Earle to square the match at 1-1.
The teams will now meet three times in 10 days with Wimbledon returning to Old Trafford for a league match on Wednesday and United coming to London for the replay the following week.
Derby and Aston Villa, who first met in the Cup in 1885, played out a one-sided Midlands derby, Derby winning 3-1 to reach the fifth round for only the third time in the past 13 seasons.
Leicester, through to the League Cup semifinals, kept alive their F.A. Cup interest with a 2-1 win over manager Martin O'Neill's former club Norwich in a match that saw both teams finish with 10 men.
Leicester's Northern Ireland international Neil Lennon and Norwich's Matt Jackson were sent off in the 34th minute after squaring up to each other.
Manchester City won their first match under new manager Frank Clark, 1-0 at Brentford, while first division Bolton were the biggest winners of the day, beating Luton 6-2 in a third round replay.
